compareCandidate.label: Chloroplast vs. mitochondrion
compareCandidate.description: Chloroplasts capture sunlight to make sugar (food) - only in plants. Mitochondria release energy from food - in all eukaryotic cells. One builds food, the other spends it.

processes: Photosynthesis: making sugar from light, water, and CO2
plainLanguageExplanation: The chloroplast is the organelle where plants make their own food. It is green because it contains a pigment called chlorophyll that captures energy from sunlight. Inside, chloroplasts have stacks of flat discs called thylakoids (grana), and the space around them is the stroma. Using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide, the chloroplast performs photosynthesis: it makes sugar (glucose) and releases oxygen. That sugar is food for the plant (and ultimately for almost all life).

whyItMatters: Chloroplasts are where plants make food from sunlight, and that food feeds almost every living thing on Earth. They also produce the oxygen we breathe. Understanding chloroplasts explains how plants grow and why life depends on photosynthesis.
tagline: The solar panel of the plant
didYouKnow: Every day, plants use chloroplasts to turn sunlight into chemical food - the process that eventually powers almost all life on Earth.
